chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAbdillāh informed me, from the one who narrated it, who said:

The world and whatever is in it belong to Allah, Blessed and Exalted, and to His Messenger, and to us. So whoever gains control over anything from it, let him have taqwa of Allah, and let him render the right of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, and let him act righteously toward his brothers. If he does not do that, then Allah, His Messenger, and we are disassociated from him.

key_terms.الدُّنْيَا: the worldly realm and its possessions
key_terms.بُرَآءُ مِنْهُ: disassociated from him and free of responsibility for him
key_terms.تَبَارَكَ وَتَعَالَى: Blessed and Exalted is He; a formula of divine glorification
key_terms.حَقَّ اللَّهِ: the due owed to Allah from one’s possessions and conduct
key_terms.فَلْيَتَّقِ اللَّهَ: let him have taqwa of Allah and act with God-consciousness

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith teach about ownership of the world and the duty to fulfill Allah’s rights?
ai.summary: This hadith states that the world and what it contains belong to Allah, His Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, and the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام. It teaches that whoever possesses worldly resources must observe taqwa, fulfill Allah’s due, and treat fellow believers well, otherwise he falls under disavowal.
